• Kenya shilling weakness – The Kenya
shilling weakened in 2022 on the back of 1) a
strengthening US dollar; 2) a strong oil price;
and 3) financing shortfalls for the budget.
The depreciation of the shilling accelerated
in Q1 2023 as inflation remained sticky and
higher-for-longer interest rates expectations
remained elevated, compounded by the risk
off sentiment triggered by the banking sector
turmoil in US and Europe.
